# Completeness Checklist: User Authentication (Register, Login, Logout, Password Reset)

**Purpose**: Check whether the auth spec is complete, unambiguous and consistent enough to move on to tasks, with extra weight on security and privacy requirements
**Created**: 2026-10-12
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md) (cross-checked against [plan.md](../plan.md), constitution v1.1.0 and PRD FR-01 – FR-03, NFR-15/17/21/22/40/41)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Requirement Completeness

- [x] CHK001 - Is the access credential lifetime (15 min) stated as a requirement, or does it exist only in Assumptions while FR-031 lists it as a configuration value? [Completeness, Spec §FR-008, §Assumptions]
  - Decision: 15 min is now a requirement in FR-008, configurable (FR-031); removed from Assumptions.
- [x] CHK002 - Is there a maximum absolute session lifetime, or can a session that renews at least every 30 days live forever? [Gap, Spec §FR-010]
  - Decision: yes, 90 days, configurable. FR-010a, FR-031, US-2 AS-9, SC-002.
- [x] CHK003 - Does the spec say whether the user is signed in after a successful password reset or must log in again? [Gap, Spec §FR-035, US-6]
- [x] CHK004 - Does the spec say whether completing a password reset on an unverified account marks the e-mail as verified, since the user just proved ownership of the inbox? [Gap, Spec §FR-034, §FR-017]
  - Decision: yes, a reset verifies the e-mail and, because that is a takeover, asks for the required consents again (as FR-022). FR-035, US-6 AS-8/AS-9, Edge Cases.
- [x] CHK005 - Are requirements defined for an e-mail typed in at the provider fallback (FR-023) that matches an existing account? Auto-linking is defined only for provider-supplied addresses. [Gap, Spec §FR-022, §FR-023]
- [x] CHK006 - Are requirements defined for a provider identity that is already linked to account A but now returns an e-mail that belongs to account B? [Gap, Spec §FR-022]
  - Decision: refuse the sign-in, change neither account; e-mail stays unique per account. FR-022a, Edge Cases.
- [x] CHK007 - Is the lifetime of pending provider data at the consent interstitial specified (how long before it is discarded if the user simply walks away)? [Gap, Spec §FR-021, US-5 AS-2]
  - Decision: 10 min, configurable. FR-021, US-5 AS-9.
- [x] CHK008 - Is lockout behaviour defined for external-provider sign-in and for password-reset requests on a locked account? [Gap, Spec §FR-012]
  - Decision: lockout also blocks provider sign-in; a reset is still allowed and clears it. FR-012.
- [x] CHK009 - Is it specified whether failed attempts during an active lockout extend the lockout or count towards a new one? [Gap, Spec §FR-012]
  - Decision: neither (default Identity behaviour). FR-012.
- [x] CHK010 - Is it specified whether the 5-attempt counter decays over time or only resets on success, lockout expiry or password reset? [Clarity, Spec §FR-012, US-2 AS-5]
  - Decision: no decay; resets on success, when a lockout triggers, and on reset (default Identity behaviour). FR-012.
- [x] CHK011 - Is logout defined for a user whose access credential has already expired but who still holds a valid renewal cookie? [Gap, Spec §FR-015]
  - Decision: accepted, logout works with the cookie alone. FR-015.
- [x] CHK012 - Is it specified whether "sign out of all devices" and password reset also clear the known-device list (so the next sign-in triggers a new-device e-mail)? [Gap, Spec §FR-015a, §FR-026]
  - Decision: yes, both clear it. FR-015a, FR-035.
- [x] CHK013 - Are retention periods defined for known devices, e-mail tokens and revoked or expired sessions, the way FR-014 defines 90 days for audit records? [Gap, Spec §FR-014, NFR-40]
  - Decision: known devices forgotten after 12 months without a sign-in (FR-026); unusable e-mail tokens deleted after 24 h; sessions deleted when revoked or expired (FR-038, FR-031).
- [x] CHK014 - Are requirements defined for which actions are audited beyond FR-014's list, or is the omission of registration, e-mail verification and reset-requested events intentional? [Completeness, Spec §FR-014]
- [x] CHK015 - Are the audit-record protection rules from constitution III (separate from application logs, per-user encryption of IP and device type, no e-mail/token in events, erasure by key deletion) captured as requirements in the spec, or only in the plan? [Gap, Spec §FR-014, §FR-030]
  - Checked: the gap was real (only plan R14 had it). Added FR-014a, worded without technology.
- [x] CHK016 - Does the spec define what the audit record of a failed login for an unregistered e-mail contains, given there is no user and the record must not hold the e-mail address? [Clarity, Spec §FR-014, Key Entities]
  - Decision: only event type, outcome and timestamp; no user, e-mail, IP or device type. FR-014, US-2 AS-6, Key Entities.
- [x] CHK017 - Is the delivery behaviour outside local development defined (e-mails silently dropped, startup failure, or something else), given FR-028 bans the console sender there and no other sender exists? [Gap, Spec §FR-028]
  - Decision: plan R11 behaviour moved into FR-028 (discard, log type + user id only, flow succeeds).
- [x] CHK018 - Are signed-in password change, e-mail address change, provider unlinking and an active-sessions list explicitly marked out of scope? [Gap, Scope boundary]

## Requirement Clarity

- [x] CHK019 - Is "special character" defined (which character set, whether Unicode letters or spaces count), and is there a maximum password length? [Clarity, Spec §FR-002]
  - Decision: any non-letter, non-digit character (spaces count); max 128 characters. FR-002.
- [x] CHK020 - Is e-mail normalisation defined beyond letter case (surrounding whitespace, Unicode/IDN domains, maximum length, accepted format)? [Clarity, Spec §FR-005]
  - Decision: trim, case-insensitive, valid format, max 256; no other normalisation. FR-005.
- [x] CHK021 - Is the SameSite mode of the renewal cookie specified? The plan picks `Strict`, the spec says only "SameSite", and the external-provider flow returns from a cross-site redirect. [Clarity, Spec §FR-008a, Plan §Constraints]
  - Decision: `SameSite=Lax`; frontend and API on the same site. FR-008a. Plan R5 to be updated.
- [x] CHK022 - Is "device type" defined with concrete values (e.g. mobile/tablet/desktop plus browser), for both audit records and the new-device e-mail? [Clarity, Spec §FR-014, §FR-026]
  - Decision: plan R6 definition moved into FR-014b.
- [x] CHK023 - Is "sign-in" in FR-026 defined to include or exclude provider sign-ins and session renewals, and does "first sign-in after registration" cover provider sign-ups as well? [Clarity, Spec §FR-026, US-7 AS-6]
  - Decision: password login, provider sign-in and confirmed provider link count; renewals do not; no e-mail after any kind of registration. FR-026.
- [x] CHK024 - Is "sign-in chain" defined clearly enough to know which sessions FR-011 revokes on reuse (one device's chain or every session of the user)? [Clarity, Spec §FR-011, Key Entities]
- [x] CHK025 - Does the 3-per-hour limit in FR-037 count the verification e-mail sent at registration, and does it apply to welcome-only and new-device e-mails? [Clarity, Spec §FR-037]
  - Decision: only reset, verification and link-confirmation e-mails are limited; welcome-only and new-device are not. FR-037. The registration e-mail counts toward the verification limit (matches plan R7); revisit if you disagree.
- [x] CHK026 - Is it specified whether a resent verification e-mail repeats the welcome text, given FR-025 requires "exactly one welcome message"? [Clarity, Spec §FR-018, §FR-025]
  - Decision: exactly one welcome message; a resend contains only the verification link. FR-018.
- [x] CHK027 - Does the provider no-e-mail path (FR-023) get the combined welcome + verification e-mail? FR-016 and FR-025 both refer only to e-mail/password registration. [Clarity, Spec §FR-016, §FR-023, §FR-025]
  - Decision: yes, the combined welcome + verification e-mail. FR-025.
- [x] CHK028 - Is it specified whether an unticked marketing consent is recorded as an explicit "false" decision? [Clarity, Spec §FR-003, §FR-004]
  - Decision: defaults to false and is recorded as an explicit refusal. FR-004.
- [x] CHK029 - Is it specified how quickly a change in verification status (FR-019) must be visible to other features, given that an issued access credential may still carry the old status? [Clarity, Spec §FR-019]
  - Decision: the lag (up to the access lifetime) is accepted because it only errs on the restrictive side; the client renews after verifying. FR-019.

## Requirement Consistency

- [x] CHK030 - US-6 says "every other session is signed out" while US-6 AS-3 and FR-035 say "all sessions are revoked" (PRD US-24 also says "all other sessions"). Which one holds? [Conflict, Spec US-6, §FR-035]
- [x] CHK031 - SC-003 requires 100% of attempts to *use* a logged-out session to fail, but FR-015 only revokes the renewal credential. Is immediate invalidation of the outstanding access credential a requirement? [Conflict, Spec §SC-003, §FR-015]
- [x] CHK032 - FR-012 requires telling the user when they can retry, while FR-013/SC-008 forbid revealing whether an e-mail is registered. Is lockout behaviour for unregistered e-mails specified so the two do not conflict? [Conflict, Spec §FR-012, §FR-013, §SC-008]
- [x] CHK033 - US-1 AS-4 refuses registration for an existing e-mail, which reveals that the address is registered. Is this enumeration path explicitly accepted, given SC-008 covers only login and reset? [Consistency, Spec US-1 AS-4, §SC-008]
  - Decision: accepted and documented in FR-005.
- [x] CHK034 - After the pre-hijack takeover in FR-022, the account keeps consents that the attacker gave. Is it specified whether the real owner must give the consents again? [Consistency, Spec §FR-022, §FR-003, Constitution III]
- [x] CHK035 - SC-001, SC-009 and SC-010 depend on client behaviour, but the plan limits this feature to the backend. Is it stated which success criteria are deferred to the frontend feature? [Consistency, Spec §SC-001, §SC-009, §SC-010, Plan §Scope]
  - Decision: deferred; note added under Success Criteria.
- [x] CHK036 - SC-002 qualifies "a device they have used before", but persistence across restarts does not depend on the device being known. Is the qualifier intended? [Clarity, Spec §SC-002]
  - Decision: qualifier dropped; SC-002 now states both limits (30 days inactive, 90 days absolute).
- [x] CHK037 - Are FR IDs ordered and grouped consistently (FR-032 – FR-037 sit before FR-025, and FR-037 covers verification e-mails but sits under Password reset)? [Traceability]
  - Checked: the order was off. Password reset moved after Privacy and FR-037 has its own "E-mail limits" group, so IDs read in order without renumbering (plan and contract keep their references). FR-010a, FR-014a/b, FR-015c and FR-022a use letter suffixes for the same reason.

## Scenario & Edge Case Coverage

- [x] CHK038 - Is behaviour defined when one device renews twice concurrently (several tabs) or loses the renewal response and retries with the old credential, which FR-011 would treat as theft and revoke every session? [Edge Case, Gap, Spec §FR-011, Edge Cases]
  - Decision: treated as reuse; only that device's session ends; client sends one renewal at a time. FR-011, Edge Cases.
- [x] CHK039 - Are requirements defined for a partial failure where the account is created but the session cannot be issued (or the reverse for reset/revocation)? [Recovery, Gap]
- [x] CHK040 - Is the user-facing behaviour defined when the session store is unavailable (login, renewal and authenticated requests)? The plan answers this (503), the spec does not. [Exception Flow, Gap]
  - Decision: 503. FR-015c, Edge Cases.
- [x] CHK041 - Is behaviour defined when a provider sign-in fails, is cancelled by the user at the provider, or returns an error? [Exception Flow, Gap, Spec §FR-020]
  - Decision: back to login with a generic message, nothing kept, audited as a failed login. FR-020, US-5 AS-8.
- [x] CHK042 - Is behaviour defined when a verification link is opened for an account that is already verified? [Edge Case, Spec §FR-017]
  - Decision: success with "already verified", whatever the link's state. FR-017, US-4 AS-2/AS-5.
- [x] CHK043 - Is behaviour defined for two registrations of the same e-mail arriving at the same time? [Edge Case, Spec §FR-005]
  - Decision: one succeeds, the other gets "already registered". Edge Cases.

## Non-Functional Requirements

- [x] CHK044 - Are rate limits defined per IP or globally for login, registration and reset/verification requests, beyond the per-account lockout and per-address e-mail limit (credential stuffing across many accounts, sign-up spam)? [Gap, Security]
  - Checked: the API already has a global limiter (per IP for anonymous requests, per user for signed-in ones, 429 `RateLimit.Exceeded`). FR-040 states that it covers every auth endpoint; no endpoint-specific limits.
- [x] CHK045 - Are latency targets defined for login and session renewal, or only for dev e-mail output (SC-006)? [Gap, Performance]
  - Decision: p95 under normal load: login and registration ≤ 1 s, renewal ≤ 300 ms. SC-011.
- [x] CHK046 - Are requirements defined for how credentials and e-mail tokens are stored at rest (hashed, never in plain text)? The plan says so; the spec does not. [Gap, Security, Constitution III]
- [x] CHK047 - Is the transport requirement (TLS 1.2+, cookie `Secure` flag) traced from constitution III into the spec? [Traceability, Spec §FR-008a]
  - Decision: HTTPS with TLS 1.2+ (PRD NFR-13) and `Secure` cookie. FR-039.

## Dependencies & Assumptions

- [x] CHK048 - Is the assumption that Facebook and X only return e-mails the user has verified backed by provider documentation, since FR-022 auto-links on it and grants account takeover of unverified accounts? [Assumption, Spec §Assumptions, §FR-022]
  - Decision: confirmed by reviewer; noted in Assumptions.
- [x] CHK049 - Is the assumption that the X app can be configured to require e-mail sharing validated with the chosen provider library? The plan lists it as a risk. [Assumption, Spec §Assumptions, Plan §Risks]
  - Decision: confirmed by reviewer; noted in Assumptions. The library mapping is still a *verify* item in plan R9.
- [x] CHK050 - Is the client-supplied persistent device identifier acknowledged as spoofable, and is that risk accepted for new-device detection? [Assumption, Spec §Assumptions, §FR-026]
  - Decision: risk accepted and documented in Assumptions.
- [x] CHK051 - Is it stated that health-data consent withdrawal (which the PRD ties to account deletion, NFR-22) is out of scope here? [Dependency, Gap, Spec §FR-003]
  - Decision: out of scope; stated in Assumptions.

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit-specify` and `/speckit-clarify`
- Several items (CHK021, CHK031, CHK038, CHK040, CHK046) are already decided in plan.md or research.md; the question is whether the spec should carry the decision as a requirement or point to it
- Highest-risk items: CHK005, CHK030, CHK031, CHK032, CHK034, CHK038
